content:
• I tried using Verso to write a blog post, but it is a bit inconvenient that when I run #eval or #check on code inside code blocks, the results are not displayed. When I write using mdgen , which I am developing, I can also see the execution results, so partly because it is my own tool, I have continued using that instead.

  • If I do not configure anything myself, the appearance is not very attractive. I also think the official reference manual was easier to read on mobile devices, and looked better, back when it used mdBook. I am sorry that this is only a rough impression, since giving concrete points for improvement would take some effort.

I think Verso is an excellent tool, and developing it is a great achievement. However, what I expected was that it would automatically generate a beautiful manual, with no configuration required, whose design was consistent with the official Lean website. I feel that this has not yet been realized.

For example, the photo above shows what happened when I tried to write a blog using Verso: the code overflows from the code block. I think it is inconvenient if users have to fix this kind of issue themselves every time.
i think maybe you can put this in the Verso channel.
This topic was moved here from #general > Complaints about Verso by Filippo A. E. Nuccio.

Sorry for the delayed reply. We have just been off at the Lean FRO off-site. I'll give a proper answer as soon as I can!

In the meantime, one clarification would be useful: what do you mean by "results are not displayed"? In the resulting HTML or the InfoView while you write?

@David Thrane Christiansen Thank you for reply.

By “results are not displayed,” I mean that I cannot check them in the editor, not in the generated HTML. In other words, yes, I mean that they are not visible in the InfoView.

I encountered a typo in an error message yesterday: DocM (Block ElabInline ElabBlock) is not registered as a a document command type`
It might be fixed already, but otherwise, hope this is useful!

Working on the mathlib phrasebook, I notice that elaboration seems to not be incremental: I see the orange bars going to the beginning of the file all the time. In my case (writing about differential geometry, a topic pretty deep in mathlib), that makes my computer run hot pretty quickly. I understand this is a "polish" kind of feature, i.e. if this is not high priority.

Trying now, I need to tweak my report a bit: elaboration goes back to the beginning of the current section --- but is really slow. Adding a single space on line 428 takes 4 seconds to rebuild --- whereas the Lean code is almost trivial (just variable statements).

This is a known limitation that I'd like to get past. Right now, Verso elaborates one top-level-element at a time, so it's rewinding to the beginning of the leanSection directive, as you observe. This isn't a fundamental limitation, but it's also not particularly trivial to overcome; thanks for reporting that it's an issue in practice for you.
Thanks for explaining! At the moment, I'm not writing lots of code in verso, so I don't mind strongly. But this would is an issue for me using verso more.
